WhyLandDData.heading: Facing these common capability issues?
description: If any of these sound familiar, you're in good company. Most enterprise L&D functions hit the same problems, and they trace to one cause: capability gets built a request at a time, with no design tying it to the business.

The parts pile up but never become a whole. Courses, a platform, competency lists and vendors all exist, yet nothing links them to a strategy or each other, so the same gaps keep reopening whatever you spend. A real learning strategy is what turns scattered activity into a function that builds capability on purpose.

maturityData.heading: The Edstellar L&D capability maturity model.
maturityData.subheading: Five stages of capability maturity. Edstellar moves your organization up the curve, level by level, until building capability becomes self-sustaining.
maturityData.expandTitle: The model is a path, not a scorecard you fill in once. Each level is a genuine step change from the one before, so here is what each stage looks like and what it takes to reach the next.

businessMeaning.title: What it means for the business.
businessMeaning.text: The higher you climb, the more it shows where the business feels it: faster reskilling when strategy shifts, stronger internal mobility and succession, and learning spend you can defend with evidence rather than activity. Near the top of the curve, capability stops reading as a cost line and starts working as a competitive edge.

levels.title: Sporadic
levels.description: Training happens on request. Someone needs a course, so one gets bought or built, but nothing ties it to the business or to the last thing you ran. Capability here is a by-product. The move to Structured begins the moment L&D gets a clear owner and a catalogue people can actually find.

levels.title: Structured
levels.description: Now there is order. Programs are organized, catalogued and delivered consistently, usually through an LMS. What is missing is direction, because the catalogue reflects what is available rather than what the business most needs. Reaching Strategic means mapping learning to a competency framework and the business plan.

levels.title: Strategic
levels.description: Learning is aligned. Every program traces to a capability the strategy calls for, and roles have defined competencies and pathways. The gap now is proof: you can say what you are building and why, but not yet what it changed. Systematic is where measurement closes that loop.

levels.title: Systematic
levels.description: Capability is managed with data. Baselines are set, impact is measured against business KPIs, and programs improve on evidence rather than opinion. The last step is as much cultural as technical, because the function starts improving itself every cycle without depending on outside help.

levels.title: Self-sustaining
levels.description: L&D runs as an engine. It senses where capability is needed, builds it, measures it and reinvests, cycle after cycle. Capability compounds, lives in how the organization works rather than in a few people, and shows up as a genuine source of advantage.

items.question: What does learning and development consulting include?
items.answer: It covers the whole learning system: strategy and operating model, content design, learning technology, governance and analytics, and delivery. Edstellar designs it, builds it and helps you run it, starting from your capability priorities.

items.question: How is L&D consulting different from a training needs analysis?
items.answer: A training needs analysis diagnoses the gaps. L&D consulting is what happens next: designing and building the strategy, content, technology and governance that close those gaps. The two connect, and Edstellar runs both.

items.question: Do you build the learning technology stack too?
items.answer: Yes. Learning Technology consulting covers LMS and LXP selection, architecture and integration, so the platforms fit your ecosystem rather than the other way around.

items.question: How do you measure L&D impact?
items.answer: Governance, Analytics and ROI consulting sets the baseline, dashboards and ROI models up front, so effectiveness is measured against business outcomes rather than activity.

items.question: Can you deliver the training, not just design it?
items.answer: Yes. Design and delivery sit under one roof: the team that designs the strategy can staff and run the programs through Edstellar's global trainer network.
